Alopecia is a medical term for hair loss, generally divided into `non-scarring (reversible) and scarring (permanent)` categories. You can explore comprehensive overviews through resources like [Types of Alopecia Explained](https://www.alopecia.org.uk/pages/category/types-of-alopecia).[[1]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)[[2]](https://theradome.com/blogs/blog/types-of-alopecia)[[3]](https://www.alopecia.org.uk/pages/category/types-of-alopecia)

### Non-Scarring (Reversible) Alopecia

- **Androgenetic Alopecia:** Also called male or female pattern baldness, this is the most common genetic and hormone-driven (DHT) hair loss. Men see a receding hairline or thinning crown; women see a widening part.[[1]](https://clarusdermatology.com/understanding-alopecia-hair-loss/)[[2]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)[[3]](https://www.suncoastskin.com/understanding-alopecia-types-of-hair-loss/)[[4]](https://theradome.com/blogs/blog/types-of-alopecia)
- **Alopecia Areata:** An autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks hair follicles, causing sudden, round, smooth bald patches. It includes variants like *alopecia totalis* (total scalp loss) and *alopecia universalis* (total body hair loss).[[1]](https://www.naaf.org/alopecia-areata/types-of-alopecia-areata/)[[2]](https://clarusdermatology.com/understanding-alopecia-hair-loss/)[[3]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)[[4]](https://theradome.com/blogs/blog/types-of-alopecia)
- **Telogen Effluvium:** A temporary shedding condition triggered by severe stress, illness, high fever, or hormonal changes causing hairs to enter the resting phase prematurely.[[1]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)[[2]](https://clarusdermatology.com/understanding-alopecia-hair-loss/)
- **Anagen Effluvium:** Rapid, diffuse hair loss during the active growth phase, most commonly caused by chemotherapy or radiation therapy.[[1]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)
- **Traction Alopecia:** Hair loss caused by chronic pulling or tight hairstyles like braids, extensions, or high ponytails.[[1]](https://theradome.com/blogs/blog/types-of-alopecia)[[2]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)
- **Trichotillomania:** A psychological body-focused repetitive behavior involving a compulsive urge to pull out one's own hair.[[1]](https://www.alopecia.org.uk/pages/category/types-of-alopecia)[[2]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)

### Scarring (Cicatricial) Alopecia

- **Central Centrifugal Cicatricial Alopecia (CCCA):** A scarring form that begins at the center or crown of the scalp and spreads outward, most frequently seen in women of African descent.[[1]](https://www.healthline.com/health/alopecia-types)[[2]](https://www.alopecia.org.uk/pages/category/types-of-alopecia)[[3]](https://harklinikken.com/blogs/journal/types-of-alopecia)
- **Lichen Planopilaris (LPP):** An inflammatory condition causing permanent hair destruction and smooth patches on the scalp, frequently affecting middle-aged women.[[1]](https://www.alopecia.org.uk/pages/category/types-of-alopecia)[[2]](https://www.healthline.com/health/alopecia-types)[[3]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)
- **Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia (FFA):** A variant of scarring alopecia causing a receding frontal hairline and loss of eyebrows.[[1]](https://www.alopecia.org.uk/pages/category/types-of-alopecia)[[2]](https://ubiehealth.com/doctors-note/types-alopecia-variants-hair-loss-info-forms-all-7114exp6)

If you or someone you know is experiencing hair loss, tell me:

- **Where** the hair loss is happening (patches, crown, hairline, all over)
- **How fast** it started

I can help you understand which specialist or evaluation steps are most relevant.

In honor of National Alopecia Areata Awareness Month, let’s talk about the different types of hair loss… because they’re not all the same, and they don’t all have the same answer. 🤍
Androgenic alopecia is genetic and hormonal, showing up as a widening part and diffuse thinning through the crown while the hairline holds. Telogen effluvium is shedding, usually triggered by a stressor that pushes a lot of follicles into their resting phase at once. Alopecia areata is autoimmune, appearing as sudden round patches, and it can affect anyone at any age. And traction alopecia is mechanical… caused by sustained pulling from tight braiding, glue, tape, and sew-ins. Reversible early, but permanent if the follicle scars.

Here’s where we fit in. Traction alopecia is the one type that’s fully preventable, and it’s exactly what our scalp-safe method was built to protect against. No glue, no tape, no tension.

Hair thinning can have very different causes, and knowing the difference matters because some forms of hair loss can lead to permanent follicle destruction.

• Androgenetic alopecia causes the follicles to gradually shrink, resulting in hairs that become finer and shorter over time, but the follicles remain intact.

• Lichen planopilaris (LPP) is a type of scarring alopecia where inflammation can destroy the follicle and replace it with scar tissue.

That distinction is important because once a follicle has been replaced by scar tissue, it cannot grow hair again.

This is why unexplained hair loss deserves a proper evaluation rather than simply relying on supplements. Early recognition and treatment can help protect the follicles you still have.
